h1: Kept Bangsaray Hotel Pattaya — a boutique seaside resort in Bang Saray where every room faces the sea
intro: Picture this: you wake up, open the balcony door, and there's the Bang Saray sea right in front of you, small fishing boats drifting in the distance, and the soft sound of waves instead of traffic — Kept Bangsaray Hotel Pattaya is a small boutique seaside resort in the Bang Saray area of Sattahip District, down the coast south of central Pattaya · it has just about 27 rooms, and every one faces the sea with a private balcony, done in a coastal style that borrows the feel of the Bang Saray fishing village · there's a beachfront pool, a fishing pier reaching out over the water where you can head out for squid jigging in the evening, and free loaner bikes for riding around the village · prices start at about THB 2,900/night, and real review scores sit around 9.1 from over a thousand guests on the major booking platforms.

body.html: An overview of who Kept Bangsaray suits — if we had to sum it up in one line, Kept Bangsaray Hotel Pattaya is a stay for people who want the sea at its quietest, not the busy, bustling side of Pattaya · the resort sits in the Bang Saray area, an old fishing village about 25 kilometres south of central Pattaya that still holds on to its traditional seaside way of life, with fishing boats, a fresh seafood market, and fairly calm water · this isn't a hundred-room high-rise with everything under one roof, but a small boutique resort of about 27 rooms that leans on privacy and atmosphere · it has been open since around 2017, converted from an older beachfront property into a coastal-style resort built around the charm of the fishing village · real reviews line up on this: the people it suits best are couples who want to escape the chaos and rest somewhere quiet, families bringing young kids for a swim in the sea close to Bangkok, and city workers who want a short seaside trip they can drive to in a single day · on the flip side, if you're after nightlife, Walking Street, or a big mall attached to the hotel, this place won't fully meet that need, because Bang Saray's selling point is quiet and nature, not Pattaya-style entertainment · put simply, Kept Bangsaray plays to "really resting" more than "having fun all night."

Location and getting there — Kept Bangsaray sits at 4/2 Moo 5, Bang Saray sub-district, Sattahip District, Chon Buri Province, directly on Bang Saray Beach · from central Pattaya it's about a 25–30 min drive south, past Jomtien and Na Jomtien · coming from Bangkok, it's roughly a 2 hr drive via the motorway, which makes it an easy short trip you can drive yourself · a big plus is that it's only about 15–20 min from U-Tapao Airport (UTP) — if you fly into U-Tapao and want to reach your stay quickly, this location is very convenient · within a short drive there's Ramayana Water Park, one of the region's large water parks, just a few minutes away, the Bang Saray seafood market, and the Khao Chi Chan viewpoint · for those without a car, the resort has a beach shuttle and can arrange transfers, but it's fair to say getting around this area is easiest with your own car or a rental, since public transport isn't as dense as in central Pattaya · one small note: if you mainly came for Pattaya nightlife, staying out as far as Bang Saray can mean long rides back and forth each night.

"I woke up, opened the curtains, and the sea filled the whole window — so quiet you could hear the waves · it's just a two-hour drive from Bangkok but it feels like a real getaway, with none of the chaos of Pattaya."

Room types and decor — being a small resort of about 27 rooms, Kept Bangsaray doesn't have dozens of room categories, but a curated few that all face the sea and come with a private balcony · it starts with the Kept Suite, a king-bed suite with a sea view, good for couples or two guests · stepping up is the Kept Family Suite, with more space and two queen beds for families · the room many people talk about is the Kept Ocean Villa, closer to the level of the pool and the sea, and the standout Kept Skyline Duplex, a two-story duplex with a wide sea view from the upper floor · the decor is an easy-on-the-eye coastal style, with white, light blue and woodwork mixed with sea and fishing-village touches, giving a clean, relaxed feel · many reviews agree that the rooms are very clean, the beds comfortable, and the sea view from the balcony worth the price, with cleanliness scores running especially high · one thing to know is that some room types, such as the duplex or rooms with a jacuzzi on the balcony, have fairly steep stairs, and some reviews note they aren't very convenient for older guests or anyone who struggles with stairs · if you're travelling with elderly companions, it's best to request a single-level room that's easy to get in and out of right when you book · another point reviews bring up often is that every room really does open onto the sea as advertised, not a sea view glimpsed through a narrow angle, which is hard to find at a stay in this price range.

Facilities, pool and activities — the most talked-about highlight of Kept Bangsaray is the beachfront pool, set facing the Bang Saray sea so that while you're in the water the sea carries on as a continuous backdrop · morning and evening are the popular times for guests to swim and take photos · there are sun loungers and umbrellas by the pool to rest under · another signature feature here is the fishing pier reaching out over the water, where guests can walk out to sit, watch the sunset, or head out for squid jigging and fishing in the evening, which captures the resort's fishing-village concept nicely · there are also free loaner bikes for riding around the Bang Saray village, a pool table, an activity table in the lobby, free parking, and free Wi-Fi · for families with kids, there's garden space and a corner where children can run around · to be honest, the pool isn't large the way a five-star resort with several pools would be, and some reviews note that the pool area is fairly open and the midday sun is strong, since there isn't much natural shade · if you go at midday when the sun is harsh, it's better to use the poolside umbrellas or swim in the morning and evening · overall the facilities here aren't about quantity, but about the seaside atmosphere and activities that fit Bang Saray.

Food and dining — the resort has its own seaside restaurant serving Thai food, seafood and international dishes, with a sea view while you eat · a point praised often in real reviews is the varied, freshly made breakfast, with both Thai and Western options, and many say the quality is better than expected for a small resort · the location helps too: because Bang Saray is a fishing village, there's fresh seafood at local prices within a short drive, and many guests head out to eat seafood at the market or a seaside spot in the village for some meals, which is part of the charm of staying here · for dinner, sitting by the sea with a cool breeze at the resort's restaurant is an atmosphere many people enjoy · one thing to know is that, being a small resort in an area that isn't crowded, the in-house dining options are more limited than at a big city hotel, so if you want more variety, plan to eat out a bit · overall, the food does well in the context of a small seaside resort, and breakfast is a point reviews mention positively fairly consistently.

Service — service is another point that draws fairly consistent praise in real reviews · being a small resort, the staff can look after guests thoroughly and warmly, and many reviews describe them as friendly, attentive and helpful — recommending restaurants, arranging transfers, and keeping the rooms in order · the small-resort feel makes you feel personally cared for rather than just a room number at a big hotel · but to be fair, a few voices in the reviews note that some of the management isn't entirely smooth — one guest said that after raising an issue they felt the team didn't respond as well as they should have, and some reviews feel the room rates are too high at certain times relative to the facilities you get · these are a minority compared with the praise, but they're worth knowing to set the right expectations · overall, service is still a strength here, especially the warmth of a small resort that's hard to find at chain hotels.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling together Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the room cleanliness that guests rate very high, sea-view rooms throughout with private balconies, the quiet calm and fishing-village atmosphere that lets you escape the chaos of Pattaya, the signature beachfront pool and fishing pier, the varied, fresh breakfast, friendly attentive staff, and a location close to Ramayana Water Park and U-Tapao Airport · On the watch-out side: the things that come up are that the water in front of the resort is fairly murky on some days, not clear like an island sea, which is typical of the Bang Saray coast in general, the open pool area with strong sun and little shade, the air-con in some rooms not getting cold enough at certain times, slow Wi-Fi in some spots, the steep stairs in some duplex rooms that aren't convenient for older guests, and some reviews feeling the price and facilities aren't quite balanced during peak periods · most of these gripes can be managed by choosing the right room, the right time, and setting the right expectation that you're coming for a quiet seaside stay, not a five-star resort packed with facilities.

"The room was very clean, lovely sea view from the balcony, sweet staff · my only gripe was that the water in front of the resort was a little murky the day we went, and the pool didn't have much shade at midday, but overall it was worth it and we really got to rest."

Price and value — the starting price for a sea-view room at Kept Bangsaray is around THB 2,900/night at normal rates, climbing to roughly THB 4,500–6,000+ over long weekends or in high season · larger rooms like the Kept Ocean Villa and Kept Skyline Duplex sit in a higher price band depending on size and timing · compared with similarly priced beachfront resorts around Pattaya–Na Jomtien, what makes Kept Bangsaray worth it is getting a full sea-view room throughout, plus the quiet calm and privacy of a small resort, which is hard to find at a stay in this price range in central Pattaya, where things tend to be crowded and busy · if you value the sea view, cleanliness and a restful atmosphere over the number of facilities, the money you spend comes back to you well · but if you expect several large pools, a full gym, a spa and multiple in-house restaurants, this price may feel less than fully satisfying compared with a big hotel · the key is to choose normal-rate periods and book ahead, since peak prices at small stays tend to climb fast given the limited number of rooms.

What to know before you book — a few things help make the stay smoother · One, if you're travelling with elderly companions or anyone who struggles with stairs, specify a single-level room without steep stairs right when you book, since some duplex rooms have fairly steep stairs · Two, set the right expectation about the sea — the Bang Saray coast is a calm Gulf of Thailand sea that's good for resting, but the water isn't clear like the Andaman or the islands, and some days it can be murky depending on conditions · Three, if you don't have your own car, plan transport ahead, ask about the resort's shuttle, or consider renting a car, since this area is easiest with a car · Four, the midday sun is strong and the pool is fairly open, so it's better to swim in the morning or evening and use the poolside umbrellas · Five, if you want an experience that fits the concept, try walking out on the fishing pier in the evening to watch the sunset, or go squid jigging after dark · Six, book ahead and compare prices across platforms, since there are few rooms and they fill quickly on long weekends — choose free cancellation first if your plans aren't set.

The verdict — from everything real reviews say, Kept Bangsaray Hotel Pattaya is the stay best suited to people who want the sea at its quietest, a sea view from every room, and a restful atmosphere near Bangkok at an accessible price · the high cleanliness scores guests give, the full sea view from the balcony, the beachfront pool, the fishing pier for squid jigging, and the warmth of a small resort give it a charm that big city hotels in Pattaya can't match · if you're looking for nightlife, a big mall attached to your stay, or a five-star resort packed with facilities, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a hotel in central Pattaya or Na Jomtien instead · but for a seaside trip where you want to escape the chaos, truly rest, and wake up to the sea every morning — Kept Bangsaray meets that need well in a way you don't often find around Pattaya, and that's why it keeps earning high review scores from over a thousand guests.

honestSummary: Kept Bangsaray Hotel Pattaya is the best stay for people who want to rest by a quiet sea, with a sea view from every room, at an accessible price near Bangkok — high cleanliness, a fishing-village atmosphere, a beachfront pool, and a fishing pier for squid jigging · but you have to accept that it's a small resort with limited facilities, the Bang Saray sea is murky on some days, and it's easiest to get around with a car.
honestChecks: If you're after nightlife and a big mall attached to your stay — Bang Saray is a quiet fishing village far from Pattaya's Walking Street → if you're mainly out at night, stay in central Pattaya or Jomtien instead.

If you expect clear island water — the Bang Saray coast is a calm Gulf of Thailand sea good for resting, and some days the water is murky depending on conditions → come for the atmosphere and the sea view, not for snorkelling over coral.
If you have elderly companions or no car — some duplex rooms have steep stairs, and this area is easiest with a car → request a single-level room, and plan the shuttle or a rental car ahead.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Kept Bangsaray Hotel Pattaya

faq.q: Where is Kept Bangsaray Hotel Pattaya · how do you get there?
faq.a: The resort is at 4/2 Moo 5, Bang Saray sub-district, Sattahip District, Chon Buri, right on Bang Saray Beach, about a 25–30 min drive south of central Pattaya · it's roughly a 2 hr drive from Bangkok, and only ~15–20 min from U-Tapao Airport · it's close to Ramayana Water Park and the Bang Saray seafood market · this area is easiest with your own car or a rental.

faq.q: Does Kept Bangsaray really have a sea view in every room · what room types are there?
faq.a: Yes — the resort has only about 27 rooms, and every room faces the sea with a private balcony · room types are the Kept Suite (King bed), Kept Family Suite (2 Queen beds, for families), Kept Ocean Villa, and the Kept Skyline Duplex, a two-story room with a wide sea view · some duplex rooms have steep stairs, so if you have elderly companions you should request a single-level room.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Kept Bangsaray · is it worth it?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 2,900/night for a sea-view room at normal rates, climbing to roughly THB 4,500–6,000+ in high season or on long weekends · the value is in getting a full sea-view room throughout, high cleanliness, and quiet calm near Bangkok · if you value the view and atmosphere over the number of facilities, it's worth it.

faq.q: What's the sea like in front of Kept Bangsaray · can you swim?
faq.a: The Bang Saray coast is a Gulf of Thailand sea with fairly calm water that's good for resting, and you can walk along the beach · but many reviews note the water is fairly murky on some days, not clear like an island sea · come for the atmosphere, the sea view, the beachfront pool and the fishing pier rather than snorkelling over coral · the resort's pool faces the sea and is comfortable to swim in.

faq.q: Who is Kept Bangsaray suited to?
faq.a: It's very well suited to couples and families who want a quiet seaside stay near Bangkok, away from the chaos of central Pattaya · you get sea-view rooms, a beachfront pool, a fishing pier for squid jigging, and bikes to ride around the fishing village · if you're after nightlife, a big mall, or a five-star resort packed with facilities, a hotel in central Pattaya may suit you better.

faq.q: What is there to do at Kept Bangsaray · is breakfast included?
faq.a: There's a beachfront pool and a fishing pier over the water to walk out on, watch the sunset, and jig for squid in the evening · there are free loaner bikes for riding around the Bang Saray village, and a beach shuttle · breakfast is included in the room rate, with both Thai and Western dishes made fresh, praised for variety and freshness · near the resort there's also fresh village seafood to head out and try.
